releases.body:
Well, you know how it goes... Misclick once and a release is sacrificed 😅 The second patch release `v3.3.3` has some more bug fixes, notably a major performance improvement for the explore page. 

## What's Changed
### 🐛 Bug fixes
* fix(mobile): show the memories date in every app language by @santoshakil in https://github.com/immich-app/immich/pull/32259
* perf(server): improve people query performance by @zackpollard in https://github.com/immich-app/immich/pull/32405

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/immich-app/immich/compare/v3.3.1...v3.3.3

releases.name: v3.3.0
releases.body:
# v3.3.0

> [!NOTE]
> We're collecting feedback related to people sharing in this discussion: https://github.com/immich-app/immich/discussions/32196 


Welcome to Immich `v3.3.0`!

This release includes people sharing, birthday memories, auto-stacked mobile edits, and a variety of other enhancements and bug fixes. Keep reading below for the full list of highlights.

## Highlights

* Shared people management
* Birthday memories
* Auto-stacked mobile edits
* Sync OAuth claims on every login
* Higher quality thumbnails and previews
* Machine learning performance and accuracy improvements (opt-in)
* New OCR models
* Notable fix: correct storage size on MacOS

### Shared people management

We are very pleased to release the next big milestone towards better sharing: people can now be shared!

As a user you can share people with another user in your cluster group:

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b011c1a2-b81c-47a8-b3d8-159d829fcf82 " =428x659")

aiSummary.oneLiner: A high-performance, self-hosted photo and video backup solution designed as a direct alternative to cloud services.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Immich is a comprehensive, self-hosted media gallery that provides seamless backup, management, and organization for personal photos and videos. It features dedicated, native mobile applications for background synchronization and a responsive web interface for viewing media across devices. The robust backend utilizes machine learning to perform automatic facial recognition, object detection, and geographical clustering entirely on your own hardware. It is specifically engineered to handle massive media libraries with high performance, efficiently transcoding videos and generating thumbnails for fast loading. It offers users complete data sovereignty and privacy without sacrificing the modern, intelligent features expected from premium cloud services.
keyFeatures: Automatic mobile backup: Seamlessly syncs photos and videos in the background using dedicated, native iOS and Android applications.
On-device machine learning: Automatically detects faces, objects, and locations for advanced search and clustering without sending data externally.
High-performance media processing: Efficiently transcodes large videos and generates optimized thumbnails to ensure fast, responsive gallery loading.
Multi-user support: Allows entire families to share a single self-hosted instance while keeping individual media libraries strictly private.
Data sovereignty: Ensures all personal media and metadata remain entirely on your own self-hosted infrastructure, maximizing privacy.

useCases.title: Cloud service migration
useCases.description: Migrating a family's entire lifetime media library away from paid, privacy-invasive cloud services to a secure local NAS.

useCases.title: Automated media archiving
useCases.description: Ensuring every photo and video taken on a mobile device is immediately, securely, and automatically backed up to a home server.

useCases.title: Intelligent photo organization
useCases.description: Utilizing built-in facial recognition to easily search for and group photos of specific family members across tens of thousands of images.

useCases.title: Shared collaborative galleries
useCases.description: Creating collaborative albums where multiple users can seamlessly contribute media from different devices into a unified collection.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Built for privacy-conscious individuals, families, and homelab enthusiasts who want a modern, feature-rich photo backup solution running exclusively on their own hardware. Users are expected to have a basic understanding of the relevant underlying technologies.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Follow the official documentation to deploy the application stack using Docker Compose.
